newsitem.title: HUNGARY: COLD SPRING GOOD FOR PRIMAGAZ, SAYS CEO.
newsitem.headline: COLD SPRING GOOD FOR PRIMAGAZ, SAYS CEO.

text.p: Increased gas sales due to an unusually cold spring made up for lower demand in January and February, Primagaz officials said at the company's annual general meeting on Friday.
"We are looking forward to a well-balanced year," Primagaz general manager Zoltan Szemmelveisz told a news conference following the company's AGM.
Primagaz is Hungary's biggest liquefied petroleum gas distributor, with a 75 percent share of the cylinder gas market and an 55 percent share of bulk gas sales in volume terms, Szemmelveisz said.
The general meeting approved the management's plan for a 17.5 percent or 175 forints per share dividend.
In 1996, the company posted a net profit of 1.58 billion forints on net sales of 17.63 billion forints compared with a net profit of 1.26 billion on net sale of 12.35 billion forints in 1995.
Figures are according to international accounting standards.
For this year Primagaz plans sales of between 20 and 22 billion forints, Szemmelweisz said.
He also said the company aims at diversifying its gas purchase sources and aims at finding cheap alternative sources.
In 1996, 80 percent of the gas Primagaz sold, came from MOL Rt , he said.
The company's 50-50 joint venture with France's Dehon will become operational by August or September, Szemmelveisz said.
The new company, Frigogaz Kft, with a capital of 45 million forints, will sell environment-friendly cooling agents that will fulfil European Union regulations to be introduced in 2002.
Primagaz's management will draw up a five to 10-year business and investment plan in 1997, Szemmelveisz said.
Primagaz is 64.7 percent owned by Netherland's Pam Gas BV, which is owned by SVH Energy NV, a subsidiary of SHV Holdings NV.
Osterreichische Kontrollbank AG holds 5.5 percent in Primagaz and Creditanstalt 4.2 percent.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Primagaz shares closed at 12,500 forints, up 500.
